memo.verdict: Neutral; park; conviction a working hypothesis. The park rule does not force the park (management C, business quality C, predictability B, trackability C); the return does: on our modal path the shares return 13.4 percent a year over eighteen months and 12.0 percent a year over three years at €133.2, against the 20 percent bar. Progress at a price below about €120 (the eighteen-month path clears 20 percent a year at €122, the three-year path at €108), or after the full-year 2026 results in late February 2027 if Transmission prints at 15 percent or better with Connect stable and the replacement Mediterranean contract signed, at which point the 'Target Setup' would be re-sorted and the multiple branch odds revised. Bearish if Connect prints below 11 percent for two halves, the replacement contract is not signed by the end of Q1 2027, or Republic Wire is written down.
case: - Thesis: Nexans is a completed self-help case riding a structural grid tailwind, priced as fair and returning too little. Seven years of selling everything that was not electrification cable took the adjusted EBITDA margin from 6.1 percent in 2020 to 11.9 percent in 2025 and ROCE from 10.2 percent to 21.3 percent, and the customer base from 20,000 to 4,000 accounts, while the sector sold out high-voltage subsea capacity to the end of the decade; at €133.2 the shares pay the stock's own median multiple for that and return about 13 percent a year on our path. Compelling below about €120 or if the company's own 2028 target proves right.

- The external change is structural, sector-wide and dated beyond the horizon, and has moved pricing power to the maker: the EU Grids Package targets €530bn to €540bn of grid investment for 2025 to 2031 (about €77bn a year); TenneT plans €65bn to 2029; Germany's capacity act of 10 July 2026 adds 11 GW; NKT's backlog is €13.5bn; average revenue per kilometre for 525 kV HVDC doubled to €1.44m for 2024 to 2026 awards from €0.62m in 2019 to 2020; utilities sign six-to-seven-year frames against two-year historically (Enedis seven-year €600m from February 2026 with doubled annual volumes). The force does not reach Connect (42 percent of H1 2026 standard sales), whose Nordic residential part is "deeply subdued with no near-term signs of recovery".

- The internal change is broad, real and mostly executed: perimeter reduction A; chief executive, other leaders, standards, new geographies, price rises, acquisitions and balance sheet all B; the screen's decision rule met twice over. Two red flags carried: the July 2026 guidance rise is "almost entirely" Republic Wire, and Republic Wire's 10.3x is a 40 percent premium to Nexans's own multiple. The next phase ("intensify") is integration, not transformation.
counter_case: - Nexans is a cyclical at a record margin dressed as a structural compounder. The 11.9 percent margin of 2025 and the 13.7 percent Transmission margin of H1 2026 were earned while high-voltage capacity was sold out and buyers paid down-payments to secure slots. Nexans, Prysmian, NKT and Asian entrants are all adding plant and vessels for 2027 to 2030; Hellenic Cables was certified for 525 kV subsea in 2026; LS Cable is building a €220m cable-laying vessel for H1 2028; a former Nexans Norway vice-president warns of structural overcapacity after 2030. The uncontracted parts of the business are already normalising: Connect's margin fell 180 bp in a year, a former Prysmian finance director expects low-voltage margins to fall from recent highs, and the July guidance raise was an acquisition, not organic. Consensus FY2028 EBITDA of €1,038m already sits €112m below the company's €1,150m target; Deutsche Bank's own FY2028 is €933m and Bernstein's stacked downside about €900m; the company itself says accelerated M&A is needed to bridge the gap. The base rate is against the buyer: on Nexans's execution stumbles the bears have been right in the short term 80 percent of the time, with 30 to 50 percent drawdowns; the architect of the turnaround left abruptly having sold shares, and the team that remains has never run this business through a downcycle. The risks research's "false friend" profile wins its own analysis of competing hypotheses: the top line will look fine (copper, Southern European volume, US consolidation) while the margin erodes underneath, and the stock at 12.4x is not cheap for that.

- Against the foundations: the moat is a shortage; the business research's own load-bearing bear case says the balance "could abruptly normalise" by 2027 to 2028, stripping pricing power and compressing margins toward history (6 to 7 percent EBITDA in 2020 on the operating line); the improvement since 2018 was authored by a chief executive who has left; the business has never held a peer-level margin.
triggers: - Progress: price below about €120 (€122 on the eighteen-month path, €108 on the three-year); or full-year 2026 results in late February 2027 with Transmission at 15 percent or better, Connect stable and the Mediterranean contract signed, at which point the setup is re-sorted and the multiple branch odds revised. An FY2026 print landing FY2027 consensus above 9.50 moves condition 2's odds toward 65 percent and the blend toward 13.6x.
- Bearish: Connect below 11 percent for two halves; the replacement contract not signed by the end of Q1 2027; a Republic Wire write-down.

- Alarm levels: Transmission margin below 13 percent in H2 2026, or an award lost to NKT or Prysmian on price; Connect below 11.5 percent for a half; European residential PMI below 45; adjusted backlog below €7.0bn; no synergy disclosure at the FY2026 results; US low-voltage prices falling with copper stable; a second slippage of GSI's survey work.
- Invalidate levels: Connect below 11 percent for two halves; the contract not signed by end-Q1 2027; a Republic Wire write-down.

- The series to watch: subsea order intake and adjusted backlog (new awards beyond mid-2028); Connect adjusted EBITDA margin; Nordic residential permits and housing starts; European residential PMIs; Republic Wire synergy realisation and the US copper-wire producer price index; LME copper; NOK/EUR. Frequency: the external series monthly or daily; segment margins and backlog half-yearly; quarterly sales in between (next 22 October 2026). Halden and mass-impregnated line utilisation are not published numbers.

- Open questions in the record: whether the discount to peers is a mispricing or a fair price for a lower margin and shorter record (we judge mostly the second); whether the Connect mix stabilises at about 11.5 percent or recovers to consensus's 13.0 percent; whether Republic Wire was a platform or a bolt-on; whether the €781k of pre-departure insider selling has an operating explanation (the board says succession; the H1 2026 results support that; the selling remains unexplained); whether the second-cheapest multiple in the set means the market is right that the good news was the base case or wrong that the stock is the theme's laggard (we lean to the first). Not assessable from the inputs: overlap with the framework's own track record and lessons files and its library of negative archetypes; the live thematics file was not among the inputs.
